headline: USA's Press Defeats Bosnia Despite Red Card and Thin Margins
story: The United States suffocated Bosnia and Herzegovina through systematic high-press intensity, winning 43 forced turnovers while maintaining a 16.2-second ball-recovery time. Bosnia dominated possession at 48%, yet USA's five-and-a-half high-press phases overwhelmed their visitors' ability to build attacks. A goal arrived on the half-time whistle; when Folarin Balogun received a red card at 64 minutes, logic suggested Bosnia might exploit the man advantage. Instead, USA's defensive discipline—anchored by Chris Richards (7.6) and orchestrated by Malik Tillman (7.9)—held firm until a second goal sealed the tie.

Bosnia's ten shots generated only 0.21 expected goals, a chasm compared to USA's 0.8. The visitors squandered a 0.21 xG chance that struck the post at 45+8 minutes; had it gone in, the narrative shifts. Tarik Muharemovic (6.9) and Ermedin Demirovic (6.6) worked tirelessly, but Bosnia's 2.4 high-press phases revealed they rarely seized the initiative. USA, despite generating lower xG than might justify two goals, converted clinical finishing into victory. The margin—clean sheet, a red card survived—belonged to a team that imposed its system and made Bosnia live inside it.

keyMoment.text: Balogun's dismissal invited chaos, but USA's press weathered the storm to claim the Round of 32.

home.verdict: Press dominance and defensive coherence converted 0.8 xG into a commanding win.
points: 5.5 high-press phases forced 43 turnovers; your front-foot aggression suffocated Bosnia's build-up play.
16.2-second recovery time held even after Balogun's 64th-minute red; Bosnia's 8.8s could not exploit the gap.
Malik Tillman (7.9) and Chris Richards (7.6) anchored the system; without their positioning, Bosnia's possession becomes dangerous.

away.verdict: Possession without cutting edge: 48% ownership and 10 shots converted to nothing.
points: 0.21 xG from 10 attempts reveals wastefulness; the 45+8' post-strike was your only genuine opportunity squandered.
2.4 high-press phases surrendered initiative; USA's press allowed no transition rhythm, no attacking momentum.
10-man USA proved more compact than 11-man Bosnia; after Balogun's 64' red, you created less, not more.

statLine: USA converted 0.8 xG into 2-0 while reduced to ten men from the 64th minute; Bosnia's 0.21 xG from 48 percent possession and 10 shots remains the match's starkest judgment.
